Covers the introduction and every section 21.1-21.14 in order (with the sub-topics Stars as Black Body Radiators, Wien's Displacement Law, Steps of Satellite Remote Sensing, Earth's Energy Budget and Energy Imbalance); numericals use values changed from the book's examples and were recomputed in Python; none repeats the chapter exercise. Book corrections followed: in F = L/4πr² r is the distance from the star (not the star's radius); Z = Δλ/λ ≈ Δf/f ≈ v/c (not '>>'); T₁ = 6000 K in Example 21.3; the cosmic microwave background (not a microwave oven) is the blackbody example; poleward-moving air runs ahead of the ground (no question uses 'lags behind').
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
